analysis.title: IG Credit Week in Review (Brad Shelofsky), 1 Nov 2026
key_insights: Week's headline moves understated the action underneath: S&P 500 -60bps, IG Corporate Index +1bp wider, CDXIG 1.5bps tighter.

GS 30y Hyperscaler basket ended the week roughly unchanged (-0.2bps) but had its most volatile week of the year, averaging 6.3bps of movement per day, nearly 3x the YTD average. Since the February launch there have been 6 days with moves of 7bps or more, 3 of them this week.

First half: a relief rally in AI credit began with short covering after META announced a ~$95bn equity financing plan (~$35bn immediate offering and a $60bn ATM program expected to begin in early 2027). Light positioning amplified the move.

Oracle's Wednesday investor day guided to positive FCF by FY2028 and about $20bn of total capital raise through FY2030, which the author calls underwhelming relative to expectations. Together with META, it played out part of the bull case: a quicker path to self-funding and less bond issuance. ORCL 6.7 56 traded at T+265bps at the Wednesday tights, 70bps tighter than Friday. The 30y basket was 17bps better from Friday's close, led by beta compression and short covering.

Second half: the rally reversed on disappointing earnings and supply from high-quality issuers. AI and cloud results were largely in line, but weakness in traditional core businesses (AMZN ad revenue, GOOGL search revenue, INTC PCs) raised concerns about growth and the operating cash needed to fund a buildout that shows no sign of slowing.
META moved to negative FCF, joining GOOGL and AMZN from last quarter. MSFT is the only hyperscaler with positive FCF.

Equity weakness was extreme: Google posted its worst day on record and NDX fell 3.5%, its largest decline since June. Combined with $25bn of Microsoft supply, the Hyperscaler basket gave back the entire first-half rally.

Primary market: issuance reached $60bn across 23 trades, nearly double the $30-35bn estimate. Microsoft's $25bn deal was its first outright deal since 2017. October closed at $132bn, in line with expectations, and YTD issuance is above $2tn, passing 2020's full-year record with two months remaining.
Global hyperscaler issuance reached $254bn, passing GIR's $250bn year-end target. Participation in the MSFT deal showed notable discipline given the broader basket of hyperscaler exposures.

Near-term view: the author expected a July-like squeeze in hypers, which came sooner and played out faster than anticipated. Risk-reward is described as fairly balanced with a bias to sell strength and rallies. Risk appetite is muted given the time of year and the forward pipeline. With the hyperscaler basket at the wides of the year, there will be moments for tactical length, especially if generic 30y IG risk is dragged wider.
